summary: The bill combats illegal unreported and unregulated fishing by directing NOAA to create and publicly maintain a blacklist of foreign vessels fleets and owners engaged in such activity or forced labor which then triggers bans on US port access territorial sea transit and seafood imports plus Treasury sanctions authority.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $20 million annually for fiscal years 2025-2030 to the Department of Commerce for implementing the IUU vessel list and related provisions, plus $4 million for a National Academies study. This represents a modest expansion of federal spending on a new enforcement and monitoring program.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or coverage.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.

Section 5 imposes visa ineligibility, inadmissibility, and revocation of entry documents for foreign persons involved in IUU fishing or related activities. This adds enforcement measures restricting entry for certain individuals.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions altering military or defense spending levels.

The bill aims to prevent IUU fishing to protect fish stocks and marine sustainability, including support for the Central Arctic Ocean Fisheries agreement. This advances environmental protection goals through international fisheries management.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to education policy or funding.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug policy or enforcement.

The bill strengthens enforcement against IUU fishing through vessel blacklisting, sanctions, port bans, import prohibitions, Coast Guard boardings, and penalties. This emphasizes stricter enforcement and punitive measures against illegal maritime activity.

The bill prohibits imports of seafood from vessels on the IUU list and authorizes sanctions blocking property and transactions. These measures restrict certain imports and impose targeted trade barriers on products linked to illegal fishing.
The bill contains no provisions addressing deficit spending or debt reduction priorities.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ rights or protections.

Section 10 encourages increased U.S. support, technical assistance, and investment in foreign nations' fisheries sectors for sustainable management and combating IUU fishing. This expands U.S. capacity-building assistance abroad.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election procedures.
The bill contains no provisions altering tech regulation or privacy standards.

The bill explicitly targets fishing involving forced labor, incorporates forced labor data into enforcement strategies, and links IUU fishing enforcement to labor abuses. This strengthens worker protections against exploitation in the fishing industry.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious liberty or anti-discrimination balances.
